page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance features a burstable CPU allocation model, 480 MB of L3 cache, and instruction set support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of DDR5 running at 7 GHz, providing a compute-focused 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-threaded throughput, registering 2,157.0 on Geekbench single-core tests and placing in the top decile for text processing workloads at 2,979.0 points. Single-threaded data compression also ranks high, reaching 34.18 GB/sec in gzip and 14.25 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-threaded metrics sit within average industry distribution tiers, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 8,369.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 15,671.17. Small model language inference achieves 272.78 tokens per second for text generation, though generation speed drops to 8.5 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The hardware configuration contains no bundled local storage and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPUs. The burstable CPU architecture combined with high-frequency DDR5 memory offers favorable compute cost efficiency for intermittent or variable loads, though sustained compute tasks may encounter resource throttling. Appropriate workloads include web serving, build and test automation, data pre-processing, text manipulation, and entry-level machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro System hypervisor, featuring an 8-vCPU, 4-core Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz alongside 16.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory. The instance features burstable CPU allocation, AVX-512 and AMX extensions, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-core performance, prominent text processing scores, and robust single-threaded compression throughput, while multi-core metrics and database tests align with average tiers. With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is suited for batch processing, web serving, software compilation, and lightweight inference jobs requiring cost-effective compute capacity.
